title: Open-source ACIS reader, kernel, and artifact-lineage refresh
mode: Deeper/broader primary-source research and implementation-readiness refinement

localScope.head: de27a33
localScope.worktreeState: The worktree was already broadly modified and uncommitted. This research pass edited only the two plan documents and added this receipt; no prior or unrelated work was staged or committed.

sources.observation: The docs.rs crate listing identifies cadmpeg-asm 0.6.1, while nested module pages served in this review still identified as 0.5.5. The documented route frames bare ASM BinaryFile4/BinaryFile8 and ACIS BinaryFile majors 217/218 and transfers supported records to a neutral B-rep representation. It does not read DWG/DXF containers or establish AcDs entity/key ownership.
sources.planDisposition: Bind CLI release, source tag, Cargo.lock, exact crate versions/features, and binary hash before any optional composed-checkpoint run. Do not equate a CLI release version with component-crate docs or assume a major/header label proves compatibility with Autodesk-modified 20800+ payloads.

sources.observation: acis-core documents typed/raw model validation and reference closure but explicitly not B-rep validity or solid construction. cq-acis converts only its documented experimental SAT/SAB profile and geometry subset through CadQuery/OCCT; unsupported body-reachable records cause conversion refusal. This shares OCCT kernel lineage with FreeCAD Part.
sources.planDisposition: Optional exact-profile parser-plus-shape route only. Require artifact/dependency identity, complete body-reachable disposition, units/tolerances, shape validity, and independently authored analytic expectations. Do not count it as an independent-kernel vote or outer DWG/AcDs reader.

sources.observation: The vendor identifies ACIS SAT/SAB import-export as a commercial component separate from the open-source OCCT core.
sources.planDisposition: Do not infer a stock OCCT/FreeCAD ACIS reader. An already-authorized commercial route remains optional and license-bound, and its shape output is OCCT-family evidence rather than an independent-kernel result.

sources.observation: OpenCADKernel labels itself early, says most operations are not written, and describes its ACIS layer through opencadcodec in the ACadRust/OpenCADStudio codec family.
sources.planDisposition: Candidate/not qualified. Revisit only after a pinned build demonstrates exercised ACIS lifting, complete admitted-body disposition, and analytic-solid tests. It cannot supply an independent outer DWG/AcDs parse.

sources.observation: Current documentation describes distinct C++ and optional legacy DXF importers, says embedded binary ACIS/SAT solids cannot currently be read, and routes DWG through an external converter to DXF followed by the selected DXF importer.
sources.planDisposition: Use only for pinned native converter/2D/explicit-entity consumer checks. Record platform, converter, backend/preferences, and imported dispositions; do not qualify ACIS semantics.

sources.observation: LibreDWG 0.14.1 NEWS records fixes for the final SAT block on 3DSOLID/REGION DXF export and SubDMesh Binary-DXF import. ACadSharp #1038 is closed and linked #1067 is listed in the v3.6.12 release history; the evolving issue includes both a caller clone/setup cause and a later writer defect for a from-scratch MESH. Current peer reports #1195, #1297, #1299, and #1321 describe distinct version/input-specific modeler omission, whole-file acceptance, spline conversion, and TABLE failure shapes.
sources.planDisposition: Retain peer reports as exact-route audit prompts only. Existing local fast owners already cover modeler continuation/cardinality, MESH, analytic spline expectations, whole-file gates, per-source block disposition, and PAR-126 TABLE fail-closed behavior. Add no duplicate issue-title tests or peer dependency.

existingOwnersRefined: PAR-07/S8: bind exact reader, crate, kernel, and CLI artifacts separately; distinguish parser closure, neutral-model transfer, shape validity, analytic expectations, AcDs association, and native consumer acceptance
Existing modeler DXF continuation and ASCII/Binary MESH owners: peer-reported final-chunk and binary-import defects are already covered; no duplicate test
Existing SPLINE, whole-file acceptance, modeler source-disposition, and PAR-126 TABLE owners: map current peer reports without importing customer drawings

sequence: Continue dependency-ready local work and reuse existing generated fast owners; treat peer issue reports as prompts, not a missing-test list.
At the existing composed PAR-07/S8 checkpoint only, select one concrete question and bind exact archive/wheel, source tag/commit, lockfile, component versions/features, runtime, and output hashes.

Admit only an exact header/dialect-matched bare SAT/SAB payload; report framing, body-reachable records, unsupported/loss accounting, neutral-model transfer, shape validity, and independent analytic metrics separately.
Keep outer DWG/DXF section extraction, handle-to-AcDs-key association, serializer preservation, and native application acceptance as independent gates.
If source/artifact/profile or platform is unavailable, record NOT_RUN/NOT_QUALIFIED and self-unblock to the next local item; do not add routine peer dependencies or full-suite runs per slice.
After implementation slices, update the owning plan/receipt, run the fast owner test, and report progress after commit.
implementationReadiness.supportBoundary: No parser pass, neutral B-rep graph, shared OCCT shape, peer issue closure, container check, or writer return promotes arbitrary ACIS, DWG AcDs association, kernel-independent geometry, FreeCAD 3D solid support, platform qualification, or any J item.

limitations: Primary-source documentation and current peer issue/release pages were reviewed online. No peer source/runtime was installed or executed, no CAD application was run, and no external drawing/corpus file was fetched. The research does not establish artifact-to-source equivalence for CADMPEG components; the plan therefore requires exact identity resolution before any optional run.
